concept: Investing on Autopilot: SIP, STP and SWP
plain_definition: Set up a SIP and explain what rupee cost averaging does and does not do
example: Suppose you receive ₹12,00,000 — a bonus, a maturity, a sale. Putting it all into equity in one day exposes the entire amount to whatever the market does next month.
risk_warning: It does not guarantee a profit. If the market falls throughout your investment period and is still down when you need the money, you will have a loss. Rupee cost averaging improves your average entry price; it does not make markets rise.

plain_definition: Not a fund manager, not an adviser, not an app, not SEBI. A guaranteed or “assured” return in the securities market is the single most reliable sign of a fraud. Bank deposits and small savings schemes carry fixed rates; market-linked investments never do. Anyone who blurs that line is telling you something about themselves.
